properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-09, about using reflow2 behind a web app. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen. DISTINCT FROM dec:live-tier, and the distinction is the whole point: that decision is about MANY WRITERS ON ONE DESIGN (the state-funeral case — thousands replanning one echeloned plan, which needs consensus and would mean replacing single-writer RocksDB). This is the opposite shape: N TENANTS, EACH WITH THEIR OWN graph_id AND ONE WRITER. No write contention, no consensus, no shared-store rewrite. The two cases share a tier and share almost none of their difficulty. THE SCALE STEPS ARE NOT EVENLY SPACED. 1k is a deployment problem and the design already points at it: cap:graph-registry (planned) specifies a bounded, evict-when-idle map from graph key to open design, and cap:select-graph-by-id (unrealized) lets a session name what it wants. Hold a few hundred designs hot, evict the rest. THE STEP CHANGE IS 1k TO 100k, and it is forced by one measured number: reflow2's OWN design is 1,828 nodes = a 3.8 MB export and a 33 MB store on disk — roughly 9x inflation, being RocksDB plus the tantivy index. At 100k tenants that is ~3.3 TB if all were resident, so the hot set is necessarily ~1% or less, which INVERTS the problem: cold open stops being an edge case and becomes the steady state. shared.rs budgets 30 SECONDS for a cold open today. The engineering question changes from 'hold many designs' (which the registry answers) to 'make opening a design cheap' (which it does not address at all). 100k TO 1M IS THEN HORIZONTAL: ~4 TB of cold blobs is unremarkable for object storage and the hot set grows with concurrency, not with registrations. A FIFTH ROAD, alongside dec:live-tier's four, and it fits what reflow2 already believes: OBJECT STORAGE HOLDS THE EXPORT AS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH, a node HYDRATES a RocksDB+tantivy cache on demand, and eviction is free because the cache is derived. This dissolves placement (any node can serve any tenant), dissolves durability (the object store's problem), and makes an idle tenant cost a ~3.8 MB cold blob instead of a 33 MB live store. reflow2 already has the primitive: the export is deterministic, sorted, content-hashed and self-contained — that IS a per-tenant blob, and the store is already derived rather than authoritative. WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING TODAY, recorded as unbuilt rather than merely absent: cap:graph-registry is planned and nothing builds it; cap:select-graph-by-id is unrealized and unverified; ver:a-session-cannot-name-another-design is PLANNED, and dec:one-process-many-stores was accepted CONDITIONAL on it, so that condition is half met; and dec:live-tier names 'no identity or authorization', which at this scale is not a gap but the product. THE FOUR WAYS TO FORECLOSE, all cheap to avoid now: (1) PROCESS-GLOBALS THAT ARE REALLY PER-DESIGN — cap:graph-registry's own text already lists graph_path, content_path, identity and write_gen as things that must become per-graph; every new static that is secretly per-design is a future migration. (2) PATH AS IDENTITY — cap:select-graph-by-id frames it correctly as 'the server maps id to path', id primary and path derived; sidecar files beside the store (.id.json, .sync.json) want to become object metadata resolved by a resolver. (3) A WHOLE-DOCUMENT WRITE ON A HOT PATH — the export being whole-document is correct for an archival action and fatal on a per-change path, which also makes BL-198 (stop serializing defaults) a SCALING decision rather than tidiness, since blob size is hydrate time. (4) BUILDING MULTI-TENANCY BEFORE PROVING ISOLATION — at this scale that is a security boundary, and retrofitting one into a running multi-tenant system is the sequencing mistake that cannot be walked back. WHAT IS NOT A PROBLEM, worth stating because it is counter-intuitive: the scaling axis is the NUMBER OF TENANTS, not the size of one design. A tenant's graph is small, so full scans, Leiden, modularity and every detector remain cheap per tenant. Single-writer-per-design is a FEATURE here rather than a limit — it is what makes N tenants embarrassingly parallel — so the box would be removing it, not keeping it. THE ONE MEASUREMENT WORTH TAKING NOW, while nothing depends on the answer: hydrate-and-index time as a function of design size (200 / 2k / 20k nodes, import to first query). Under a second for a typical tenant and the cache model is routine engineering; seconds and a read model in front becomes necessary — and that is better known before designing around the opposite assumption.
properties.name: OPEN — what does reflow2 look like at 1k / 100k / 1M tenants each holding their OWN design, and what must not be foreclosed now?
properties.rationale: Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the thinking survives without being claimed as intent. Kept SEPARATE from dec:live-tier rather than appended to it, because one node holding two questions can only ever be half-answered and these two differ in their hardest part: many-writers-one-design needs consensus, many-single-writer-tenants needs cheap hydration. Worth keeping even if none of it is built, for three reasons: the 9x store-to-export ratio is a measured anchor that decides the architecture and was not previously written down anywhere; the fifth road follows from a primitive reflow2 already has rather than from new invention; and the four foreclosures are cheap now and expensive later, which is exactly the class of thing a design graph exists to hold. Anthony's framing was explicitly about not painting into a corner rather than about building this, and the record should keep that distinction.
